prerequisites: Previous participation in the "Chemie" (Chemistry) module is desirable.

learning_outcomes.text: Students know common coating processes and their application possibilities in mechanical engineering.
Students are familiar with methods for characterizing coatings and can apply them to evaluate the quality of layers.
Students know the application-specific properties (e.g., regarding corrosion protection, wear protection) of coated surfaces.
Students can weigh which coating technology is suitable depending on the substrate and future operating conditions.
Independently develop complex problem solutions and present the results in a report.
Work on technical issues in a team.

syllabus_topics: Pre-treatment, intermediate treatment, and post-treatment of surfaces
ECD (electrochemical deposition) with and without external current
Application-specific properties (e.g., wear and corrosion protection) of coated surfaces
teaching_methods: Project work (usually carried out in the lab)
assessment_rules: The module is graded based on a seminar paper. To pass, a minimum of 50 out of 100 points must be achieved on the seminar paper.
bibliography: Klaus-Peter Müller, Praktische Oberflächentechnik, Vieweg Verlag
Kirsten Bobzin, Oberflächentechnik für den Maschinenbau, Wiley-VCH
Hansgeorg Hofmann und Jürgen Spindler, Verfahren in der Beschichtungs- und Oberflächentechnik, HANSER-Verlag
